scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: A single IT Department workstation, it_lab3 (192.168.1.x),
"is totally isolated" -- the user says it can't reach anything at all, not even its
own gateway, and suspects the machine lost its network or its switch port died.
Please find and confirm the fault on it_lab3 and tell us what to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
I validated the it_lab3 host itself and the local IT LAN. On it_lab3 (192.168.1.5/24), eth0 is UP with carrier (LOWER_UP), correct IP and default route via 192.168.1.1. Layer‑2 is healthy: ARP to the gateway succeeds (arping returns replies from c2:fe:97:68:52:b9), and the neighbor table shows the gateway reachable. Layer‑3 is also normal: it_lab3 can ping its gateway (192.168.1.1), a same‑LAN peer (it_lab1, 192.168.1.3), and a different subnet host (office_pc, 192.168.3.2) without loss. From the LAN side, a reverse ping from it_lab1 to it_lab3 also succeeds. This proves the switch port, cabling/L2 segment (lan_it), and routing via the gateway are functioning.

No blocking firewall is present (iptables chains are ACCEPT). The networking.service on these containers shows “inactive (dead)” by design (one‑shot), and this matches other healthy IT hosts, so it is not a fault.

Root cause: No current network fault on it_lab3; the reported isolation cannot be reproduced and may have been transient or application/DNS related.

Corrective fix: No restart is required. If the user still observes issues, have them retry using IP addresses. If symptoms recur, a harmless local refresh would be to bounce the interface (ip link set eth0 down; ip link set eth0 up) or systemctl restart networking, but the network is presently healthy.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent confirms it_lab3 holds 192.168.1.5/24 and can ping its gateway 192.168.1.1 (ARP replies and pings succeed 'without loss'), matching the baseline-healthy note.

The agent's investigation log contains concrete observations (interface up, correct IP, default route, successful pings between hosts) that support the conclusion that it_lab3 is not isolated.
